summary: Cherokee County, NC lookout built 1940, NHLR-registered 1997; standing and renovated 2023, not run regularly since 1993, opened only on announced fall days.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register lists Cherokee County as administrator. The 2019 Forest Service release and the 2023 news stories describe the Tusquitee Ranger District of the Nantahala National Forest running the open days and completing renovations. The record keeps the Register's field; the Forest Service role is in the agency fact.

The Register names no builder. The 2019 release credits the Civilian Conservation Corps. Blue Ridge Public Radio says it was built as a lookout for the NC Forest Service. Both can be true: a CCC crew may have built a tower for the state forest service.

The Register and the 2023 Smoky Mountain News say the tower is still used in periods of high fire danger. The 2023 Blue Ridge Public Radio story says it has not been operated on a regular basis since 1993. Sources disagree on how active it is.
The Register gives an elevation of 2,264 ft (690 m), which matches the brief. The 2019 release calls the summit 2,293 feet. The record keeps the Register figure.

notes_for_editor: Story sources are 2019 and 2023 items; no 2024-2026 status found, so the access note should be rechecked with the Tusquitee Ranger District before anyone visits. The brief's agency field comes from the Register's administrator line and differs from the Forest Service sources. Staffing and current-use claims conflict across sources; the story says so. Facebook posts that appeared in search results were not used because they were not fetched.
